sentence.8544: title: Latin American Governments Targeted By Ransomware url: https://www.recordedfuture.com/latin-american-governments-targeted-by-ransomware Recorded Future examined the recent escalation of cyberattacks on Latin American (LATAM) governments from January 2022 until May 2022.
sentence.8545: We analyzed vulnerabilities, attack vectors, and indicators of compromise (IOCs), identified the most prevalent ransomware gangs targeting LATAM governments, and highlighted the lack of proper cybersecurity hygiene in the region.
sentence.8546: This report includes information gathered using the Recorded Future Platform, dark web sources, and open-source intelligence techniques (OSINT).Executive SummaryWe identified several government entities in Latin America (LATAM) that have been affected by ransomware attacks, likely involving Russian or Russian-speaking threat actors, beginning on or around April 2022.
sentence.8547: Countries affected include Costa Rica, Peru, Mexico, Ecuador, Brazil, and Argentina, among others, all of which have publicly condemned Russia for invading Ukraine at the United Nations General Assembly (UNGA).
sentence.8548: Some of these countries also voted to suspend Russia from the United Nations Human Rights Council (UNHRC) in early April 2022.
sentence.8549: More recently, national emergencies have been issued regarding these attacks, such as in Costa Rica.
sentence.8550: Ransomware groups involved in these attacks against governments in LATAM include Conti, ALPHV, LockBit 2.0, and BlackByte.
sentence.8551: We have anecdotally identified a noticeable increase in initial access brokerage (IAB) services on top-tier Russian-language dark web and special access forums such as XSS and Exploit advertising low-cost, compromised network access methods related to entities in LATAM.
sentence.8552: We have also observed several high-profile database leaks related to entities in LATAM on low-tier and mid-tier English-speaking forums such as BreachForums, with data dumps spiking in April 2022.
sentence.8553: Additionally, we observed a significant increase in the sale of compromised credentials affecting LATAM government domains on dark web shops in Q1 and Q2 2022, relative to 2021.
sentence.8554: These observations and trends could represent a paradigm shift in the ransomware and broader cybercriminal community related to unwritten rules and internal group policies on the targeting of government entities.
sentence.8555: Key JudgmentsThe credibility of ransomware attacks on LATAM government entities is high, based on analysis of leaked sample data, threat actor indications, and historical activities, patterns, and trends related to tracked ransomware operators and affiliates.
sentence.8556: If unaddressed, ransomware attacks on local, provincial, or federal government entities in LATAM could constitute a credible national and geopolitical security risk.
sentence.8557: Entities in LATAM will remain attractive targets for ransomware operators and affiliates, as the region lacks the proper cybersecurity education, hygiene, and infrastructure to defend against such threats.
sentence.8558: If attacks on LATAM government entities were to escalate to target infrastructure and critical services, this would pose a significant national security risk.
sentence.8559: The most likely attack vectors employed by ransomware affiliates targeting LATAM government entities include the use of compromised valid credentials obtained via infostealer infection, initial access broker sale, or purchase on a dark web shop or marketplace.
sentence.8560: The targeting of LATAM government entities could represent an initial shift away from internal cybercriminal policies on the targeting of governments worldwide.
sentence.8561: Threat AnalysisAttack VectorsAs of May 26, 2022, we can not definitively determine the attack vector employed by ransomware operators and affiliates targeting LATAM government entities.
sentence.8562: However, the most common method by which threat actors obtain initial access to networks is through the use of compromised valid credential pairs (T1078) and session cookies (T1539), which are often harvested from a successful infostealer infection (T1555, T1083) and sold by specialized initial access brokers on dark web and special-access sources.
sentence.8563: This is the most likely avenue by which such threat actors gained access to compromised LATAM government networks.
sentence.8564: These infostealers are often spread via phishing (T1566), spamming, the unintentional downloading of a malicious (T1204) or masquerading (T1036) file, and various other methods.
sentence.8565: We have observed a minor, sustained increase in references to initial access sales and database leaks targeting LATAM government entities on dark web and special-access sources, beginning in approximately March 2022.
sentence.8566: These observations are recorded anecdotally via Insikt Groups daily threat leads, analyst notes, and reports.
sentence.8567: We have observed several threat actors, such as zirochka, on top-tier Russian-language forums XSS and Exploit auctioning compromised network accesses targeting entities in LATAM in bulk for relatively low prices (< $100).Figure 1: Timeline of ransomware attacks on LATAM government entities, mapped to references to LATAM on dark web and special-access sources (Source: Recorded Future)We have observed a slight increase in database dumps related to LATAM government entities, beginning in March 2022 and spiking on April 4, 2022.
sentence.8568: We have also identified a significant increase in Q1 2022, beginning in February 2022, of references to domains owned by government entities in LATAM on dark web shops and marketplaces such as Russian Market, Genesis Store, and 2easy Shop, relative to the same time period in 2021.
sentence.8569: These dark web shops and marketplaces specialize in the sale of compromised account credentials, remote desktop protocol (RDP) and secure shell (SSH) accesses, and infostealer malware logs that can be utilized to gain access to a victims network.
sentence.8570: While we cannot determine any direct or causal link between the increased supply, frequency, and volume of advertisements targeting government entities and domains in LATAM to ransomware attacks targeting LATAM government entities, we believe that such trends and observations warrant further research to analyze and determine any possible correlation.
sentence.8571: Figure 2: Examples of bulk initial access auctions targeting unspecified entities in LATAM (Source: Exploit Forum)Ransomware Gangs Targeting LATAM Government EntitiesWe have observed at least 4 high-credibility ransomware gangs targeting LATAM government entities during a period of time beginning on April 1, 2022.
sentence.8572: These gangs include Conti, ALPHV (BlackCat), LockBit 2.0, and BlackByte.
sentence.8573: These incidents constitute a significant escalation in the severity and impact of ransomware targeting.
sentence.8574: Generally, ransomware affiliates avoid targeting healthcare facilities, K-12 educational institutions, international organizations and coalitions, and local, provincial, or federal governments.
sentence.8575: The risk of negative publicity and stigmatization on dark web and special-access forums, mainstream media attention, and international law enforcement activity increases dramatically once targets in these industries are attacked.
sentence.8576: It is possible that the targeting of LATAM entities by presumably Russian or Russian-speaking ransomware gangs could mark the beginning of a paradigm shift in which targets that were previously internally sanctioned by the group could now become viable targets for ransomware operations.
sentence.8577: ContiThe most noteworthy of these targets is the attack on the government of Costa Rica by Conti, which resulted in the worlds first nationwide emergency declared as the result of a ransomware attack.
sentence.8578: The attack, likely perpetrated and publicized by ransomware affiliate or affiliate group unc1756, also likely known as wazawaka, has garnered widespread media and law enforcement attention.
sentence.8579: Since affiliates often work independently from the larger ransomware brand, it is possible that the attacks on Costa Rica that were claimed by Conti are not the work of the larger group.
sentence.8580: Conti has claimed to have exfiltrated, encrypted, or destroyed approximately 1TB of sensitive information related to the administration and operations of several Costa Rican entities including the Ministry of Finance (hacienda[.]go[.]cr), the Ministry of Labor and Social Security (mtss[.]go[.]cr), the Development Fund and Family Allowances Bureau (fodesaf[.]go[.]cr), and the Interuniversity Headquarters of Alajuela, Costa Rica (siua[.]ac[.]cr).
sentence.8581: Previous Conti posts also made vague references to controlling public utilities such as water and electricity, likely indicating indirectly that the group had access to Costa Rican industrial control system / supervisory control and data acquisition (ICS/SCADA) environments.
sentence.8582: However, we are not able to verify these claims.
sentence.8583: Conti followed their claims of an attack on Costa Rica with an attack on Peru that affected the General Directorate of Intelligence (digimin[.]gob[.]pe) and Ministry of Economics and Finance (mef[.]gob[.]pe).Figure 3: Announcements of attacks on Costa Rican and Peruvian government entities by the Conti Gang (Source: Conti.News)ALPHV (BlackCat)On April 16, 2022, the ransomware gang ALPHV (BlackCat) leaked an unspecified amount of compromised data related to the Municipality of Quito, Ecuador (quito[.]gob[.]ec).
sentence.8584: This marked the first time that ALPHV targeted a government entity located in LATAM.
sentence.8585: According to Ecuadorian media, this attack took several services offline for an unspecified amount of time.
sentence.8586: This is a noteworthy event, as the Mayors Office of Municipality of Quito and State Attorney Generals Office confirmed that the initial attack caused the suspension of several critical government services, which caused an inconvenience to users who have not been able to carry out procedures.
sentence.8587: As of April 25, 2022, all of the information claimed to have been exfiltrated by ALPHV is available to download for free on a .onion domain provided on the public-facing ALPHV extortion website with the same name.
sentence.8588: Compromised information likely includes sensitive financial, legal, and political documents related to the operations and administration of the Municipality of Quito, Ecuador.
sentence.8589: This information, if leveraged by an opportunistic threat actor, criminal, or nation-state, could prove to be damaging to Ecuadors national security.
sentence.8590: Figure 4: Announcements of an attack on the Municipality of Quito, Ecuador from the BlackCat Ransomware Group (Source: ALPHV)LockBit
sentence.8591: 2.0On May 23, 2022, the LockBit 2.0 ransomware gang published to their blog leaked files related to the Secretary of Health of the State of Morelos, Mexico (saludparatodos[.]ssm[.]gob[.]mx), a breach that was initially disclosed on or around May 16, 2022.
sentence.8592: This disclosure followed a previous claim on April 22, 2022 that LockBit 2.0 had compromised the network of the Secretary of State for Finance of Rio De Janeiro, Brazil (fazenda[.]rj[.]gov[.]br).
sentence.8593: Neither of these incidents were widely reported in either Mexican or Brazilian media.
sentence.8594: As of April 25, 2022, it is unclear whether the attacks resulted in a significant disruption of critical services related to the government entities.
sentence.8595: Additionally, also as of April 25, 2022, all of the information claimed to have been exfiltrated by the LockBit 2.0 ransomware gang is available to download for free on the public-facing LockBit 2.0 extortion website called LockBit 2.0 Leaked Data.
sentence.8596: The compromised information likely includes sensitive financial, legal, and political documents related to the operations and administration of these entities.
sentence.8597: This information, if leveraged by an opportunistic threat actor, criminal, or nation-state, could prove to be damaging to the national security of Mexico and Brazil.
sentence.8598: Figure 5: Announcements of attacks on Mexican and Brazilian government entities by the LockBit Gang (Source: LockBit Blog)BlackByteOn May 21, 2022, the BlackByte ransomware operators published claims on their public-facing extortion website named BlackByte Blog that they had compromised the internal network of the Comptroller General of the Republic of Peru (contraloria[.]gob[.]pe).
sentence.8599: As of April 25, 2022, the BlackByte ransomware operators have not published any noteworthy data related to this government entity.
sentence.8600: This attack has yet to be confirmed by any representatives of the Comptroller General of Peru and has not been extensively reported on in Peruvian or Spanish-language media.
sentence.8601: As of this writing, we cannot determine if this attack caused the disruption of critical services provided by the comptroller general, although it is likely that any detected service disruptions on the domain are related to this attack.
sentence.8602: Figure 6: Announcement of an attack on a Peruvian government entity by the BlackByte Ransomware Gang (Source: BlackByte Blog)Cybersecurity Hygiene and Trends in Latin AmericaAlthough most countries in LATAM have adopted a national cybersecurity strategy, there is still much work yet to be done in terms of improving the cyber capacity and security posture in both the private and public sectors; at the moment, only 3 LATAM countries (Brazil, the Dominican Republic, and Mexico) are members of the 30-plus-country ransomware task force.
sentence.8603: The most effective investment would be to give residents in LATAM and the Caribbean in-person or remote access to IT security-oriented schools and training institutions.
sentence.8604: Educational and training institutions in the region simply cannot keep up with the current demand for IT security professionals.
sentence.8605: Investments in education, training, and apprenticeship programs would make the most difference in building capacity, closing the cyber skills gap, and getting more individuals into the cyber talent pipeline.
sentence.8606: Supporting and encouraging younger individuals to seek an education and training within the cyber realm can drastically affect the skills shortage and improve public awareness on cyber threats; the region has been particularly affected by cybercrime and fraud during the pandemic.
sentence.8607: While it is difficult to evaluate countries given their alternative approaches to cybersecurity, some have decided to leave cybersecurity to private firms while others have leaned on government agencies and the military to combat cybercriminals.
sentence.8608: According to the Organization of American States (OAS) cybersecurity observatory, most LATAM countries are in the early stages of cybersecurity development.
sentence.8609: As a result, there is still a lot to accomplish and implement in terms of cyber security policies in Central American and Caribbean countries.
sentence.8610: Nevertheless, countries such as Argentina, Dominican Republic, Ecuador, Panama, and Peru, among others, are making significant efforts to advance their cyber capabilities.
sentence.8611: However, there is a small list of countries with established policies, legal frameworks, institutional capacity, and human capital resources, including Brazil, Uruguay, Colombia, and Chile.
sentence.8612: And although they are still developing, countries such as Brazil, Colombia, Chile, and Mexico have taken the lead in broadening their institutional capacities, including the development of cyber laws, policies, and regulations.
sentence.8613: There is also increased expertise in the private sector, primarily the financial sector, within these nations.
sentence.8614: MitigationsIt is crucial to maintain offline backups of your organizations data and ensure that these backups stay up to date to prevent data loss in the event of a ransomware infection.
sentence.8615: Additionally, we recommend the following mitigations to reduce overall risk and impact:Ransomware often follows a specific pattern of behavior that can be detected with a robust threat intelligence system that is integrated with SIEM platforms.
sentence.8616: Implement YARA rules such as the ones found in Recorded Future Hunting Packages to identify malware via signature-based detection or SNORT rules for endpoint-based detections.
sentence.8617: The IOCs provided throughout this report can be used to proactively query or scan environments for items such as file hashes, registry keys, and IP traffic associated with ransomware.
sentence.8618: Network segmentation can halt the propagation of ransomware through an organizations network.
sentence.8619: This solution involves splitting the larger network into smaller network segments and can be accomplished through firewalls, virtual - local area networks, or other separation techniques.
sentence.8620: Implement intrusion detection / intrusion prevention (IDS/IPS) systems and endpoint detection and response (EDR) systems.
sentence.8621: Provide robust anti-phishing training for employees and staff.
sentence.8622: If remote access solutions are crucial to daily operations, all remote access services and protocols such as Citrix and RDP should be implemented with two-factor or multi-factor authentication.
sentence.8623: Exposed RDP servers are also abused by threat actors to gain initial access into a targets network.
sentence.8624: Threat actors will look for networks that have internet-facing servers running RDP and then exploit vulnerabilities in those servers or use brute force password attacks.
sentence.8625: Once inside the network, the threat actors move laterally and install ransomware on target machines, often disabling backups and other protections.
sentence.8626: Through the use of process monitoring, monitor for the execution and command of binaries involved in data destruction activity, such as vssadmin, wbadmin, and bcdedit.
sentence.8627: Monitor for the creation of suspicious file modification activity, particularly large quantities of file modifications in user directories.
sentence.8628: Consider keeping sensitive client information on systems that are disconnected from the internet or segmented from the rest of the corporate network.
sentence.8629: Since ransomware will encrypt all files on a victim system and often will search for directories on the network (such as networked file shares) to also encrypt, moving highly sensitive customer data to a system with no internet access or access to the rest of the network will minimize ransomwares access to those files.
sentence.8630: OutlookRansomware will likely continue to be incorporated into the attack methods of threat actors targeting public and private entities in LATAM due to their availability as ransomware-as-a-service (for non-technical threat actors) and highly successful infection rates.
sentence.8631: Compromised accounts and networks are highly sought after by threat actors and will remain in high demand because they can be used in a number of attack vectors, including but not limited to account takeovers, identity theft, social engineering, credential stuffing, and brute forcing.
sentence.8632: As LATAM is an up-and-coming region whose security posture is not as sophisticated or developed as some other regions for various reasons (geopolitical circumstances and developing infrastructure, among others), threat actors may view LATAM entities as easy targets for harvesting sensitive and financially lucrative accounts via infostealer infections.
sentence.8633: As incident response teams in the region build up their security posture, threat actors are likely to continue to enhance and create infostealer variants to target organizations in LATAM with the intent of harvesting personal and corporate account login details and other important data.
sentence.8634: title: Chinese Threat Actor Used Modified Cobalt Strike Variant to Attack Taiwanese Critical Infrastructure url: https://blog.eclecticiq.com/chinese-threat-actor-used-modified-cobalt-strike-variant-to-attack-taiwanese-critical-infrastructure Executive Summary EclecticIQ researchers identified a malicious web server very likely operated by a Chinese threat actor used to target Taiwanese government entities, including critical infrastructure.
sentence.8635: The command-and-control infrastructure was publicly exposed to the internet.
sentence.8636: Based on log and meta data found on the server, EclecticIQ analysts assess with high confidence the threat actor performed offensive cyber operations, including reconnaissance, malware delivery, and post-exploitation against selected targets.
sentence.8637: EclecticIQ analysts identified a modified version of Cobalt Strike known as "Cobalt Strike Cat"[1].
sentence.8638: Researchers analyzed these logs and created a detailed map of the adversary's tactics, techniques, and procedures (TTPs).The threat actor primarily focused on exploiting four different remote code execution (RCE) vulnerabilities to target web services and heavily relied on open-source tools, some of which are exclusively available in Chinese underground forums.
sentence.8639: The threat actor also engaged in brute-forcing against the victim's internal web services.
sentence.8641: Offensive Tooling EclecticIQ analysts discovered a web server with the IP address 156[.]251[.]172[.]194, which was accessible to the public.
sentence.8642: The server contained HTTP header data (SimpleHTTP/0.6 Python/3.8.10), indicating the use of a Python library called SIMPLEHTTPSERVER to serve the files and folders detailed in Figure 1. Figure 1 – Screenshot of exposed threat actor infrastructure showing available tools and target lists..
sentence.8643: EclecticIQ analysts identified post-exploitation and reconnaissance tools on the server.
sentence.8644: Most of the tools are open source.
sentence.8645: Based on the event logs within a modified version of Cobalt Strike, analysts have determined with high confidence that Mandarin was set as the default language.
sentence.8646: The identified tools include: Afrog: Vulnerability Scanning for Penetration Testing [2] CIPR:
sentence.8647: Converting domain name to IP address [3] Neo-reGeorg: Reverse proxy tool [4] Nuclei: Vulnerability scanner
sentence.8648: [5] OneForAl: Subdomain collection tool [6] Fscan: Reconnaissance tool
sentence.8649: [7] LaZagne: Recover stored passwords on a system [8] SharpCheckInfo: Situation awareness tool [9] HackBrowserData: Decrypting and exporting browser data [10] FRP: Reverse proxy tool
sentence.8651: [12] Targeted Attack Lifecycle The Targeted Attack Lifecycle is a methodology to map adversary tactics, techniques, and procedures (TTPs) in a structed way.
sentence.8652: EclecticIQ analysts mapped identified TTPs to each phase of the life cycle (Figure 2) - beginning with the threat actor´s infrastructure (156[.]251[.]172[.]194) and continuing with the different tools used by the actor to compromise systems and perform lateral movement.
sentence.8653: Figure 2 – Targeted Attack Lifecycle of the threat actor.
sentence.8654: Reconnaissance of Exposed Webservices The threat actor utilized reconnaissance tools to scan and fingerprint systems exposed to the internet.
sentence.8655: In some cases, the actor used a preconfigured (hard-coded) target lists, which is showing the intended victims.
sentence.8656: EclecticIQ analysts validated many of these targets as real and existing systems.
sentence.8657: Figure 3 shows an example of a target list created by the attacker, which mainly contains Taiwanese government entities.
sentence.8658: This list served as input for OneForAll - a subdomain enumeration tool.
sentence.8659: Figure 3 – Files inside the exposed infrastructure under the OneForAll file path.
sentence.8660: After enumerating subdomains of the associated victim network, the threat actor uses automated vulnerability scanning tools including Nuclei and Afrog to identify potentially exploitable systems.
sentence.8661: Figure 4 shows final report logs from Afrog and Nuclei found on the attacker infrastructure.
sentence.8662: The threat actor utilized virtual sandboxes named "Test" to demonstrate cyber-attacks before executing them on a real victim device.
sentence.8663: The IP addresses observed in these virtual sandboxes are tied to the same computer name, identified as DESKTOP-0TBCAC4.
sentence.8664: The adversary also demonstrated an interest in exploring the public-facing network surface of public transport and utilities industries.
sentence.8665: Figure 4 – Completed reconnaissance and vulnerability scans.
sentence.8666: Initial Compromise Through Exploiting Publicly Facing Applications
sentence.8667: The threat actor utilized automated vulnerability discovery and reconnaissance techniques to scan a given target list, refine the selection and identify potential exploitable systems before commencing the attack.
sentence.8668: Based on evidence obtained from the bash history data, EclecticIQ researchers observed that the threat actor primarily focuses on four different known remote code execution (RCE) vulnerabilities during their operations:• CVE-2023-21839 Oracle WebLogic Server RCE
sentence.8672: [16] Figure 5 – BASH history logs of from the threat actor’s system showing exploitation of CVE-2020-2551.
sentence.8673: Establish Foothold by Modified Version of Cobalt Strike The threat actor utilized a modified version of Cobalt Strike 4.5, dubbed "Cobalt Strike Cat", to create a dedicated communication channel from the victim system and perform evasive post-exploitation steps.
sentence.8674: Cobalt Strike Cat was initially shared on a Chinese-speaking cybersecurity forum called t00ls[.]com, with a link to a GitHub repository and was distributed inside an encrypted ZIP folder.
sentence.8675: Only registered users of t00ls[.]com could obtain the decryption key for the ZIP folder and access the tool.
sentence.8676: Notably, t00ls[.]com is a private forum that can only be accessed by individuals who possess invitation codes for the site.
sentence.8677: Figure 6 – “I want to become a master hacker”.
sentence.8678: Publication of Cobalt Strike Cat on t00ls[.]com.
sentence.8679: Figure 7 – Example user interface of Cobalt Strike Cat shared on a GitHub repository.
sentence.8680: Notable features of Cobalt Strike Cat include: 1.
sentence.8681: Evasion techniques to specially bypass Anti-Virus solution “360 Total Security”, which is a Beijing, China-registered internet security company mostly used in Asia-Pacific region.2.
sentence.8682: Option to use Google 2FA key during login to the command-and-control server as an attacker for further operational security.
sentence.8683: 3. Modified stager designed to evade signature-based detection during malware execution.4.
sentence.8684: Patch for publicly available Cobalt Strike vulnerability tracked as CVE-2022-39197 [17].Figure 8 shows a small portion of Cobalt Strike Cat logs from the attacker´s infrastructure.
sentence.8685: According to log data, a reverse shell was established from the remote victim device as SYSTEM-level privileges using a process named "bea.exe".
sentence.8686: The attacker then changed the Cobalt Strike Cat beaconing frequency for behaviour-based evasion by sending the "sleep 10" command to the infected host and executed the "tasklist /SVC" command to list all running processes on the victim device.
sentence.8687: Figure 8 – Sample of Cobalt Strike Cat logs.
sentence.8688: The result of the "tasklist" command shows that the victim was using a commercial software called SONAS
sentence.8690: SONAS is an application for remote monitoring and control of Internet of Things (IoT) hardware devices.
sentence.8691: Analysts assess with high confidence that the compromised device was used to access CCTV cameras of the Directorate General of Highways in Taiwan.
sentence.8692: Analysis showed that the victim IP address was publicly serving a web service that contained a phpMyAdmin database.
sentence.8693: The database used a weak password and was susceptible to brute-force attacks.
sentence.8694: Figure 9 shows the redacted victim DNS address, confirming that the web service was used by the Taiwanese government.
sentence.8695: The IP addresses and the computer name matched the victim device name in the Cobalt Strike Cat logs.
sentence.8696: Figure 9 – PHPINFO page from victim web service.
sentence.8697: Internal Reconnaissance to Identify Lateral Movement Opportunities EclecticIQ researchers observed multiple internal network reconnaissance attempts after initial compromise.
sentence.8698: These attempts are primarily performed with an open-source automated vulnerability scanning and brute forcing tool called FSCAN.
sentence.8699: Figure 10 showed that the threat actor used FSCAN (named as f.exe) to find possible vulnerabilities on internal network of infected device which can be used by threat actor to perform lateral movement: Figure 10 – Usage of FSCAN on a victim’s network.
sentence.8700: EclecticIQ researchers observed that the threat actor used the Windows command-line arguments to perform general reconnaissance against infected devices.
sentence.8701: The following commands were identified: Command Line Argument Description query user || qwinsta Display information about logged-on users and their sessions.
sentence.8702: net user Displays information about user accounts.
sentence.8704: "DBPath" *.* Used to search for the string "DBPath" in all files within the current directory and its subdirectories. arp –a Address resolutions for remote systems. netsh wlan show profiles Display a list of all the wireless network profiles.
sentence.8705: dir %APPDATA%\Microsoft\Windows\Recent List of recently opened files and folders on the computer.
sentence.8706: Figure 11 shows some examples of commands executed by the threat actor on an infected host: Figure 11 – Executed reconnaissance commands on infected host.
sentence.8707: Escalate Privileges with Stolen Credentials The threat actor uses stolen passwords from valid accounts as the primary vector for privilege escalation.
sentence.8708: The actor deployed various credential stealing techniques against compromised hosts to obtain user account passwords in NTLM hash format and saved credentials from web browser.
sentence.8709: These passwords would allow the threat actor to escalate privileges using valid accounts if the accounts were privileged .
sentence.8710: The Cobalt Strike Cat beacon logs (Figure 12) show that the actor uploaded LaZagne onto the infected device for credential harvesting purposes and deleted the LaZagne binary after execution to avoid detection from the user's side.
sentence.8711: EclecticIQ researchers observed LaZagne uploaded from the attacker device (“C:\Users\Test\Desktop\ONE-FOX集成工具箱_V1.0魔改版_by狐狸\gui_other\Cobalt_Strike_4.5\plugin\TaoWu\script\lazagne.exe”) to the victim device file path C:\Windows\Temp.
sentence.8712: The actor leveraged ONE-FOX - a collection of pentest tools - to copy binaries from actor´s system to the victim. Figure 12 – Threat actor successfully obtained user account credentials in NTLM format.
sentence.8713: The threat actor utilized an open-source tool called HackBrowserData to export victim browser data, including passwords, history, cookies, bookmarks and download records from several web browsers.
sentence.8714: Figure 13 – Execution of Hack-browser-data on infected host.
sentence.8715: Maintain Presence via Windows Service Installation To establish persistent remote access on the victim device, the threat actor abused Windows services to install modified version of Cobalt Strike payload.
sentence.8716: Windows services ran with the highest privilege, NT AUTHORITY\SYSTEM and execute the malware automatically during system startup, allowing for remote access to the victim device with persistence.
sentence.8717: Malicious service installation is accomplished via the below command line argument: sc create WindowsUpdate binPath= C:\Windows\Temp\svchost.exe start= auto obj= LocalSystem DisplayName= windowsupdate When this command is executed on remote victim device, it will install a fake Windows service called “windowsupdate”.
sentence.8718: This service executes a malicious binary (Cobalt Strike Cat payload) under “C:\Windows\Temp\svchost.exe” every time the victim device is started.
sentence.8719: Figure 14 – Installation of malicious Windows service.
sentence.8721: Trough Reverse Proxy The threat actor utilized open-source reverse proxy tools to expose local devices located behind a NAT or firewall, to the Internet.
sentence.8722: This allowed the attacker to conduct vulnerability scans, general reconnaissance, and brute-force attacks on systems attached to the internal network of the infected device.
sentence.8723: Threat actor uploaded the fast reverse proxy (FRP) binary to the "C:\Windows\Temp" file path and then executed it on victim machine.
sentence.8724: Figure 15 displays the reverse SOCKS proxy activity on the infected device using the open-source tool FRP.
sentence.8725: FRP received a command-line argument from attacker used to establish a connection from the adversary-controlled infrastructure (156[.]251[.]172[.]194) over port 2333.
sentence.8726: Figure 15 – Execution of FRP reverse SOCKS proxy on infected host.
sentence.8727: After establishing the reverse SOCKS proxy connection, the threat actor performed internal reconnaissance and brute forcing attempts on some of the internal FTP servers inside victim network. Victimology and Targeting Patterns EclecticIQ researchers assess with moderate confidence that the primary targets of the threat actor are Taiwanese government entities and organizations in the critical infrastructures sector.
sentence.8728: Logs obtained from attacker infrastructure, such as target lists and metadata show that organizations in Taiwan account for the largest proportion of targets.
sentence.8729: According to event logs, on 02/09 at 08:51:43 UTC, EclecticIQ researchers have concluded with high confidence that the actor compromised an IOT device in the network of the Directorate General of Highways, MOTC in Taiwan
sentence.8731: After this initial comprise the threat actor performed reconnaissance and credential harvesting from infected host, very likely to perform lateral movement as an end goal.
sentence.8732: Although the majority of activity was directed at Taiwanese government entities, researchers also observed other separate target lists containing IP addresses and domains associated to government websites from Egypt, Malaysia, Dominican Republic and the UAE also targeted recently by this threat actor.
sentence.8733: Figure 16 – Reconnaissance against Malaysian and Egyptian government entities.
sentence.8734: The reconnaissance against Malaysian and Egyptian government entities was carried out using a generic Python script that contained an author comment section with the handle "mwxiaojia."
sentence.8735: However, there is no distinct evidence to conclusively attribute the cyber operations to an individual using that persona.
sentence.8736: Attribution EclecticIQ analysts assess with moderate confidence that the infrastructure was operated by a Chinese threat actor.
sentence.8737: Analysts identified the following findings supporting the assessment: The modified version of Cobalt Strike event logs obtained from the threat actor infrastructure revealed additional IP addresses that very likely belong to the attacker and metadata that very likely show the origin of the attacker.
sentence.8738: File and folder names, file content and comments in threat actor tools were written in Mandarin.
sentence.8739: The timezone of attacker virtual sandbox 103[.]156[.]184[.]83 is in the UTC+08:00 timezone.
sentence.8740: This time zone is used in all predominantly Chinese-speaking regions.
sentence.8741: Every successful login attempt made by the attacker using the default Cobalt Strike username 'neo' to access the command-and-control server was logged, along with the attacker's IP address.
sentence.8742: EclecticIQ researchers observed that the threat actor used private proxy addresses from a Chinese underground proxy IP solution called 'Tigercloud Club' to conceal their real IP address.
sentence.8743: Some of tools used by the actor are exclusively available in Chinese underground forums.
sentence.8744: The identified adversary TTPs overlap with a previously known Chinese APT group called Budworm [20].
sentence.8745: Cobalt Strike Cat event logs: Figure 17 – Event logs from Cobalt Strike Cat showing details about victim and threat actor.
sentence.8746: Figure 18 – Event logs from Cobalt Strike Cat showing details about the testing sandbox used by the threat actor.
sentence.8747: Mitigation and Prevention Strategies One of the main initial access vector is exploitation of publicly exposed web services.
sentence.8748: EclecticIQ researchers recommend limiting the remote access of publicly available web services and consistently monitoring and installing available patches.
sentence.8749: Reconnaissance attempts on publicly exposed web services can be detected and stopped using a combination of techniques, such as: • Log analysis:
sentence.8750: Monitoring and analyzing logs generated by the web server can help identify abnormal traffic patterns, such as repeated attempts to access a specific resource or an unusually high volume of requests from a single IP address.• Network traffic analysis: Network traffic analysis can help identify traffic that is not legitimate or is attempting to scan the network or web services.• Intrusion detection systems: Deploying an intrusion detection system (IDS) can help identify and alert administrators to malicious activities such as port scans or network sweeps.• Web application firewalls: Web application firewalls (WAF) can be used to protect web services from reconnaissance attempts by blocking or limiting access to resources and detecting and blocking known malicious patterns in web traffic.
sentence.8751: The threat actor used a variation of Cobalt Strike as a command and control (C2) server to send malicious commands into infected computers.
sentence.8752: Some tips to help prevent such C2 connection attempts: • Monitor network traffic:
sentence.8753: Monitor network traffic regularly to detect unusual activities or traffic patterns that may indicate C&C connections.• Deploy firewalls:
sentence.8754: Deploy firewalls to block traffic from known C&C domains or IP addresses.
sentence.8755: The threat actor installed a second stage persistence backdoor on infected device by abusing Windows Services.
sentence.8756: The actor then tried to dump User Account credentials via SAM database and attempted to access saved browser credentials.
sentence.8757: There are several ways to use Windows Group Policy to avoid these kinds of post exploitation attempts: •
sentence.8758: Disable the "Create global objects" user right:
sentence.8759: This user right allows non-administrative users to create global objects, including services.
sentence.8760: By disabling this user right, you can prevent non-administrative users from creating services.• Restrict access to the Security Accounts Manager (SAM) file: The SAM file contains sensitive information, including user account passwords.
sentence.8761: By default, only the SYSTEM account has access to the SAM file.
sentence.8762: However, an attacker who gains administrative access to the system can potentially dump the SAM file and extract password hashes.
sentence.8763: Restrict access to the SAM file, you can use the "Deny access to this computer from the network" user right.
sentence.8764: By denying network access to the system, you can prevent attackers from using network-based attacks to dump the SAM file.• Disable password saving in web browser using Group Policy.

sentence.8818: title: Open-Source Gh0st RAT Still Haunting Inboxes 15 Years After Release url: https://cofense.com/blog/open-source-gh0st-rat-still-haunting-inboxes-15-years-after-release/ Found in Environments Protected By: Proofpoint By Nathaniel Raymond, Cofense Intelligence Gh0st RAT, a decades-old open-source remote administration tool (RAT), recently appeared in phishing campaigns targeting a healthcare organization.
sentence.8820: Remote Administration Tool was created by a Chinese hacking group named C. Rufus Security Team that released it publicly in 2008.
sentence.8821: The public release of Gh0st RAT source code made it easy for threat actors to obtain and tailor the tool to their needs.
sentence.8822: Its feature set expanded over the years to include various surveillance, persistence, and information-stealing capabilities: Taking full control of the infected machine Recording keystrokes in real time with offline logging available Accessing live web cam feeds including microphone recording Downloading files remotely Remote shutdown and reboot Disabling user input Over Gh0st RAT’s long life, Chinese nation-state threat actors have used it to breach high-value targets such as governments, embassies, economic targets, and media.
sentence.8823: One such breach was the operation known as “GhostNet” in 2009, in which a large-scale cyber-attack used Gh0st RAT to conduct surveillance and espionage.
sentence.8824: The breach impacted the Dalai Lama’s Tibetan exile centers in multiple countries.
sentence.8825: Although Gh0st RAT was first identified in reports of threat activity almost 15 years ago, it is still actively distributed today.
sentence.8826: Cofense Intelligence identified an email targeting a European-owned medical technology organization located in China, attempting to deliver Gh0st RAT via an embedded link.
sentence.8827: The embedded link that hosted the malware was affiliated with Tencent and based in Hong Kong.
sentence.8828: The sample’s command and control (C2) server is also located on the CHINANET Jiangsu province network in the city of Nanjing.
sentence.8829: Figure 1: A screenshot of the recent phishing email used to deliver Gh0st RAT via an embedded link.
sentence.8830: Figure 2: A translation of the body of the recent Gh0st RAT campaign shows that it used an unpaid invoice as a theme.
sentence.8831: Although Ghost RAT has a history of use by nation-state threat actors, Cofense Intelligence does not have conclusive evidence that this recent campaign is associated with known nation-state activity.
sentence.8832: The activity we observed activity shares certain characteristics with some advanced persistent threat (APT) groups, including APT27, which is known for intellectual property theft against healthcare and technology companies, and is also known for the use of Gh0st RAT.
sentence.8833: However, since Gh0st RAT’s source code is publicly available, it remains plausible that any threat actor could download and modify the code for their own needs.
sentence.8834: With Chinese universities (including more than one in Nanjing) being heavily involved in training talent for the Chinese defense industry, it is also plausible that students or other threat actors that are at times associated with APT groups may be carrying out independent threat activity using tools they are familiar with.

sentence.8867: title: CrowdStrike Uncovers I2Pminer MacOS Mineware Variant url: https://www.crowdstrike.com/blog/i2pminer-macos-mineware-analysis/ CrowdStrike analyzed an I2Pminer variant that targets macOS
sentence.8868: The mineware utilizes I2P to hide XMRig network traffic The CrowdStrike Falcon:registered: platform provides continuous protection against mineware threats by offering real-time visibility across workloads CrowdStrike recently analyzed a macOS-targeted mineware campaign that utilized malicious application bundles to deliver open source XMRig cryptomining software and Invisible Internet Protocol (I2P) network tooling.
sentence.8869: Research began after identifying suspicious multi-architecture binaries within a public malware repository.
sentence.8870: Analysis of common samples shows that the techniques in this campaign date back to the summer of 2021.
sentence.8871: The identified applications shared a common theme: identifying as Apple Logic Pro X, Final Cut Pro, Traktor or various Adobe Creative Suite products.
sentence.8872: The primary executable is a dropper containing a legitimate version of the application and I2P tooling.
sentence.8873: Utilizing I2P, the dropper then downloads a custom XMRig miner and orchestrates the mining operations.
sentence.8874: Open source reporting1 also observed similar usage of I2P and XMRig, but the previous threats did not involve the same usage of a legitimate application and scripts to deploy its tooling.
sentence.8875: The CrowdStrike Falcon platform provides continuous protection against cryptomining threats by delivering real-time visibility across workloads to protect customers.
sentence.8876: Technical Analysis This campaign lures the victim into believing that they are installing a legitimate application for successful execution.
sentence.8877: The malicious dropper contains a legitimate version of the software and executes it to give the illusion of a properly behaving application.
sentence.8878: It then relies on a number of shell scripts to configure and orchestrate its mining operations.
sentence.8879: The following analysis was performed on a binary that drops and executes a copy of Apple Logic Pro X (bfa9f7b8014efab4143fb2a77732257144f3b804ee757fb41c9971b715da53d7).
sentence.8880: Installation It is likely that these malicious application bundles are distributed via Apple Disk Images (DMGs).
sentence.8881: The malicious application bundles were observed executing out of the /Applications/ folder.
sentence.8882: DMGs are a common delivery mechanism for both benign and malicious software.
sentence.8883: It is typical for DMGs to instruct users to drag and drop application bundles from the mounted disk image to the application folder.
sentence.8884: Dropper Binary At the core of these malicious application bundles is a Mach-O binary acting as a dropper.
sentence.8885: Binaries were found to be universal Mach-Os, supporting both x86_64 and ARM architectures.
sentence.8886: The dropper binary is located within the installed application bundle at /Applications/Logic Pro X.app/Contents/MacOS/Logic Pro X.
sentence.8887: Therefore, it executes when the application bundle is launched.
sentence.8888: The dropper is responsible for orchestrating the installation and execution of the legitimate application, I2P tooling and XMRig miner.
sentence.8889: Figure 2 outlines the multiple layers of process execution.
sentence.8892: Throughout the dropper’s lifecycle, it heavily relies on randomly generated names for folders and files in the /tmp/ directory.
sentence.8893: The dropper binary generates a number of these file paths through its own random character generator and dynamically produces the script content with these generated values.
sentence.8894: The scripts also rely heavily on the usage of mktemp to generate variables within the scripts.
sentence.8895: Both of these methods produce files with the syntax of ._[a-zA-Z]{8} (e.g., ._JdYdPLMq).
sentence.8896: Files produced within the Mach-O are generated with 10 characters, whereas usage of mktemp within the scripts produces files made of eight characters.
sentence.8898: In order to appear as a working copy of Logic Pro X, the dropper contains a legitimate copy of the lure application.
sentence.8899: The dropper starts by generating a script to decode the legitimate Mach-O file.
sentence.8900: During this process a large Base64-encoded file is written to disk.
sentence.8901: An example of this script can be found in the Appendix.
sentence.8902: Its purpose is to create a mirrored application bundle located in the host’s /tmp/ directory.
sentence.8903: The mirrored bundle contains the legitimate application instead of the dropper binary.
sentence.8904: The generated script is executed via a /bin/sh subprocess.
sentence.8905: The script removes any files that conflict with its randomly generated paths.
sentence.8906: Then it creates a new folder structured for the bundle located at /tmp/._[a-zA-Z]{10}/Logic Pro X.app/Contents.
sentence.8907: It creates symbolic links in the /tmp/ bundle to mirror all directories found in /Applications/Logic Pro X.app/Contents and /Applications/Logic Pro X.app/Contents/MacOS to their respective /tmp/ locations.
sentence.8908: All files located in /Applications/Logic Pro X.app/Contents folder are copied to their respective /tmp/ location.
sentence.8909: The Logic Pro X dropper binary is deleted with the /tmp/ bundle.
sentence.8910: It will be replaced with the legitimate application.
sentence.8911: In order to unpack the legitimate binary, the previously written Base64 file is decoded and unarchived.
sentence.8912: The contents are saved to /tmp/._[a-zA-Z]{10}/Logic Pro X.app/Contents/MacOS/Logic Pro X.
sentence.8913: The script’s final action is to set the executable bit of this binary.
sentence.8914: The dropper then forks itself in order to launch the legitimate application.
sentence.8915: The forked process makes a call to execl to execute the legitimate Logic Pro X application located in /tmp/.
sentence.8916: The original dropper process continues to execute in order to orchestrate the mining operations.
sentence.8917: It relies on two additional scripts to configure the I2P network tooling and download the XMRig mining software.
sentence.8918: I2P Dropper Script I2P is an anonymous network layer.
sentence.8919: All communications over I2P are anonymous and end-to-end encrypted, and users of the network don’t reveal their real IP addresses.
sentence.8920: The dropper binary unpacks a customized Mach-O compiled from the open source i2pd (I2P Daemon) project.
sentence.8921: Usage of i2pd enables other processes on the computer to tunnel traffic to the I2P network.
sentence.8922: I2P is configured and used by the dropper to download the mining tooling but also to proxy the miner’s network communications.
sentence.8923: The I2P dropper script is written to disk at /tmp/._[a-zA-Z]{10}.
sentence.8924: An example of the script can be found in the Appendix.
sentence.8925: The script is executed as a /bin/sh subprocess.
sentence.8926: The script first deletes itself from the disk.
sentence.8927: This is done to evade detection but also to open up the opportunity to reuse the same randomly generated filename for the actual i2pd binary.
sentence.8928: The i2pd binary is stored within the script as a large, inline Base64-encoded variable.
sentence.8929: This value is decoded and the output is written to an additional file (/tmp/._[a-zA-Z]{8}).
sentence.8930: This file is read and unarchived to the original file path of the I2P dropper script.
sentence.8931: The script pads the resulting Mach-O with a random number of \x00 bytes.
sentence.8932: The padded i2pd Mach-O file is executed via a call to exec -a "/System/Library/Frameworks/CoreServices.framework/Frameworks/Metadata.framework/Versions/N/Support/mdworker_shared" "$0" Note that $0 will resolve the first argument of the current process.
sentence.8933: This is the file path of the I2P dropper script, which was replaced with the padded i2pd Mach-O file.
sentence.8934: The exec call will execute the binary and modify the process name to the mdworker_shared file path.
sentence.8935: After the process executes, the I2P dropper script removes the i2pd Mach-O file from the disk.
sentence.8936: i2pd The I2P Daemon binary dropped by the Logic Pro X dropper is tooling built using version 2.41.0 of the open source project.
sentence.8937: It is a universal binary supporting both x86_64 and ARM architectures.
sentence.8938: Public i2pd binaries rely on config files or command line arguments for necessary configuration of tunnels and upstream connections.
sentence.8939: The binary used in this threat is custom tooling developed on top of the i2pd code base.
sentence.8940: In addition to running the I2P network stack, it also contains static configuration elements necessary for the operation of the XMRig miner.
sentence.8941: This allows it to minimize command line arguments and additional files dropped to disk.
sentence.8942: The custom binary is built to configure two tunnels from the local host to the I2P network.
sentence.8943: These tunnels are responsible for the localhost listeners on ports 4444 and 4445.
sentence.8944: The listener utilizing port 4444 is called “pool” while the listener utilizing port 4445 is labeled “payload.”
sentence.8945: These align with their usage by the XMRig downloader and miner.
sentence.8946: Each tunnel is configured to tunnel traffic to an upstream address within the I2P network.
sentence.8947: The following chart summarizes the tunnels and their configurations.
sentence.8948: Label Type Local Address Local Port Destination Address pool client 127.0.0.1 4444 hghsfkrat5dd7ikqzk3d3h5jattjxlru6zmxzxd7y3wib6goodmq.b32[.]i2p payload client 127.0.0.1 4445 jiasil3a7kcxitu4swlixbnyt6wbbm65kqknqknnvkj2yvj7lliq.b32[.]i2p
sentence.8949: The host now has a running i2pd process.
sentence.8950: This will enable it to use the I2P network for the XMRig download, and to handle the miner’s network communications.
sentence.8951: XMRig Downloader Script XMRig is an open source CPU/GPU miner that supports numerous protocols.
sentence.8952: The dropper generates and executes a script to download, configure and execute a copy of a XMRig miner.
sentence.8953: The script is executed as a command line argument passed into a /bin/sh -c
sentence.8955: This script is executed by the Mach-O dropper before the I2P Dropper script, but its first step is to sit in a loop and wait for the creation of the /tmp/i2pd directory.
sentence.8956: This directory is generated during the execution of the I2P Dropper script.
sentence.8957: After this file is detected, the XMRig downloader starts a second I2P Daemon process and saves the new pid to /tmp/i2pd.
sentence.8958: The script then removes any files that conflict with its randomly generated paths.
sentence.8959: The script then enters a download loop that contains two subloops, one to download the MD5 hash of the XMRig payload, and a second to download the XMRig payload.
sentence.8960: During the first subloop, curl is used to download a MD5 hash from http://127.0.0[.]1:4445/updtmd.
sentence.8961: This localhost port is configured to tunnel traffic through i2pd to the destination address listed above.
sentence.8962: This loop attempts the download every five seconds until it is successful.
sentence.8963: During this loop, the script implements a check using pgrep for Activity Monitor processes in an attempt to evade user detection.
sentence.8964: If Activity Monitor is detected then execution is stopped and the script exits.
sentence.8965: If the MD5 hash is successfully downloaded, its value is saved and execution is passed to the second subloop.
sentence.8966: This second subloop performs the same actions but instead pulls the XMRig payload from http://127.0.0[.]1:4445/update.
sentence.8967: If this download is successfully written to disk, it is hashed and the value is compared to the previously downloaded MD5 hash.
sentence.8968: If the hashes are equal, execution proceeds past the download loop — otherwise, the outer download loop is reevaluated.
sentence.8969: The XMRig payload is then extracted from the download via tar, and the resulting Mach-O file is padded with a random number of \x00 bytes.
sentence.8970: Similar to the ip2d process, it is executed via an exec -a call utilizing a process name of /System/Library/Frameworks/CoreServices.framework/Frameworks/Metadata.framework/Versions/N/Support/mdworker_local Next, the XMRig Download Script sends the XMRig miner a config via the XMRig miner’s native API.
sentence.8971: In order to accomplish this, curl is used to send a post message to http://127.0.0[.]1:4543/1/config.
sentence.8972: Port 4543 is the default listening port for XMRig’s API.
sentence.8973: An example of this config can be found in the Appendix.
sentence.8974: The script enters a final loop to once again check for the presence of an Activity Monitor process.
sentence.8975: If Activity Monitor is running, the script kills the I2P Daemon and XMRig miner processes and exits.
sentence.8976: XMRig The XMRig binary dropped by the Logic Pro X dropper is also custom tooling built using version 6.18.1 of the open source project.
sentence.8977: This is also a universal binary supporting both x86_64 and ARM architectures.
sentence.8978: The binary’s source is modified to execute with an altered default configuration.
sentence.8979: Similar to the I2P Daemon, this is done to minimize command line arguments.
sentence.8980: The binary does not need a command line miner config.
sentence.8981: The http API is also enabled by default.
sentence.8982: This is done so that no configs need to be passed via the command line and that the config can be sent via curl within the XMRig download script.
sentence.8983: The config also reveals a few details about the mining operations.
sentence.8984: The existence of a donate-over-proxy value and the usage of generic user and password values within the XMRig configuration reveal the usage of a mining proxy.
sentence.8985: The usage of a proxy allows authors to control all of their mining implants and their target pools via a centralized console.
sentence.8986: This proxy server is located on the I2P network at the destination of the pool tunnel.
sentence.8987: The XMRig implant will execute until the user logs off, shuts down their computer or opens Activity Monitor.
sentence.8988: With the observed configuration, it will utilize the I2P network and the mining proxy to perform CPU mining operations on the host.
sentence.8989: Defense Evasion The dropper binary and its scripts utilize a number of techniques to avoid detection.
sentence.8990: The dropper bundle in the applications folder appears legitimate, and this bundle houses all of the Logic Pro X dependencies/frameworks.
sentence.8991: The authors cleverly utilized these legitimate dependencies via symbolic links when dynamically creating the legitimate bundle in the temp folder.
sentence.8992: Even though the scripts produce many on-disk artifacts, the dropper and scripts are quick to remove them as soon as they are executed or used.
sentence.8993: The i2pd and XMRig binaries are padded with a random number of zero bytes to change its hash and expand its size.
sentence.8994: They also both use CoreServices framework binaries as the execution name.
sentence.8995: This is so that it can blend in within process tree/process viewers.
sentence.8996: Mining-related CPU spikes can be difficult to notice due to the system resource-intensive applications that were chosen.
sentence.8997: If these spikes are noticed, the implant is also quick to kill itself and clean up its on-disk artifacts if it determines the user is investigating system resources via Activity Monitor.
sentence.8998: Persistence The dropper does not establish persistence through typical means, instead relying on the lure of its legitimate application for execution.
sentence.8999: The mining infrastructure is dropped, downloaded and deleted every time the dropper executes.
sentence.9000: As long as the dropper successfully launches its legitimate application, the user will continue to execute the dropper under the assumption that it is legitimate.
sentence.9001: Dropper Variant A related group of dropper variants was also identified (e.g., 27158886ab064880aa5d5196248f2ad4b20b38bbb1321f72bca17351165ea3e5).
sentence.9002: These variants are distributed by a malicious application bundle that contains a setup script, legitimate application and Mach-O dropper.
sentence.9003: All three files are distributed within the Contents/MacOS directory in the application bundle.
sentence.9004: The setup script is the app bundle’s primary executable and serves to execute the legitimate binary, copy the Mach-O dropper to /tmp/._[a-zA-Z]{10} and execute the relocated Mach-O. Similar to the techniques and analysis above, the Mach-O dropper installs i2pd and the XMRig miner.
sentence.9005: The variants utilize the same variable names and directory naming schema, and also date back to Summer 2021.

sentence.9065: title: Evasive NoEscape Ransomware Uses Reflective DLL Injection url: https://blog.cyble.com/2023/06/04/evasive-noescape-ransomware-uses-reflective-dll-injection/ New Ransomware-as-a-service (RaaS) Targeting Vmware ESXi Servers Recently, Cyble Research & Intelligence Labs (CRIL) detected the emergence of a fresh Ransomware-as-a-Service (Raas) initiative called ‘NoEscape.’
sentence.9066: This program was discovered to be promoted on a cybercrime forum towards the end of May 2023.
sentence.9067: The creators of NoEscape were actively seeking affiliates to join their network.
sentence.9068: CRIL has shared the details of this discovery through the latest blog post.
sentence.9069: Following that, EVIL RABBIT, a security researcher on Twitter with the handle @D4RKR4BB1T47, recently shared a tweet featuring a picture of the dashboard panel used by the NoEscape ransomware group.
sentence.9070: The figure below shows the post by security researcher EVIL RABBIT.
sentence.9071: Figure 1 – NoEscape RaaS Affiliate Panel (Source: EVILRABBIT)
sentence.9072: In addition to sharing the dashboard panel image, the security researcher also provided images of the RaaS builder page and accompanying samples associated with this specific ransomware family.
sentence.9073: The affiliate website of NoEscape RaaS offers a range of executable building options, including EXE and DLL files for Windows 7 and above, reflective DLL injection for Windows 7 and above, executable files for Windows XP, and ELF executables for Linux/ESXi servers.
sentence.9074: The affiliate page includes instructions for customizing the ransomware executables, such as specifying the ransomware name, ransomware key name, comment, price or ransom amount, and timer type (None, double, or leak).
sentence.9075: According to the provided screenshot, the NoEscape RaaS platform offers affiliates the option to choose between generating a single encryption key for all binaries or creating distinct keys for each individual binary.
sentence.9076: This flexibility allows affiliates to tailor their approach and encryption strategy based on their specific requirements or preferences.
sentence.9077: The ransomware builder interface allows affiliates to configure various settings for building the ransomware executables.
sentence.9078: These settings include specifying the size of large files where partial encryption is applied instead of encrypting the entire file, defining the primary path for encryption, specifying file paths to skip during encryption, targeting specific services and processes, configuring autorun entries, enabling auto ransom note opening, and even changing wallpapers on infected systems.

sentence.9082: UAC BYPASS After creating the mutex, the ransomware modifies specific registry values to disable User Access Control (UAC), a security feature in Windows.
sentence.9083: UAC prompts users for permission or administrator credentials before allowing actions that could affect system settings or files.
sentence.9084: By deactivating UAC, the ransomware gets elevated privileges without requiring user permission or administrator credentials.
sentence.9085: This enables the malware to carry out malicious activities on the system without difficulty, posing a significant risk to the system’s security.
sentence.9086: EnableLUA By modifying the below registry value EnableLUA to “0”, malware aims to deactivate User Account Control (UAC) on the target system.
